title: Riverboat dance schedule, intermissions and ticket prices

blocks.x: Well, you see, you're playing, I was talking for my time.

You start the plane on that boat at eight o'clock. And the boat leaves out at nine, and the people come on that dance. Well, you take your little trip up the river, and you dance all the way up the river, see. You go up about, you go up about little pass, West Wegoes Ferry, you know where that's. You go past that. You go up there about, you know where that, there was no bridge there, you know where that bridge that, what's they call that bridge up there? Long, sleepy, long bridge. Well, there was no bridge. You go up about that far, see. See, you go up about that far. Well, the boat, just be, this barrel turned over, this, this, this, this, going this fast, not to keep the current of the waterfall pushing down, this, this whole bridge, this way it slopes the river. See. Now, she go up the river, and she get back at eleven o'clock. See. At eleven o'clock that gangplank, rain, that bell ring. So the whole thing took three hours.
I mean, you played for three hours.

Yeah, you played for three hours. The trip was two hours. Yeah, you played. See, but every, every now, it's ten minutes in the mission. See, that's for them to buy soldiers and stuff. You take two ten minutes in the hour, take two ten minutes. Now that's for people to eat, dance, and play, and candy wheel, you know. See. That's the way you play it. And you do it every night on a Sunday, on a Saturday. Played a candy wheel? Yeah. What was that? It's a wheel just like a roll-head wheel. You put all your number, you put a box of candy. Oh, it's like a side show or something. Yeah. Big wheel? Yeah, it's a big wheel and you put your quartet on, you pick out your number you want. See. Because they have that on the board. And on a Saturday you play as a matinee, that's from two to six. And then at night do you. Then you come back at eight o'clock, you play this night. And some Sundays they have what you call an all day ride. You play a Sunday, you play a matinee every Sunday evening. Well an all day ride starts in the morning at nine o'clock, boat leave at nine o'clock. Well at nine o'clock when that boat ready, they leave that boat and load it. Sometimes I didn't turn them back. See, the five hundred was all she was supposed to carry, she was carrying more natural time. See. You used to load that boat up to, you know how far that boat stood out of the water? Yeah. They would have people on that boat that are water meters like this. Oh yeah? Yeah.
They must, the Stratford must make good money on that.

Sure. And, but see when I was on that boat it wasn't 50 cents a coming, 50 cents a night, dollar on a Saturday and Sunday. See. All day rides was a dollar. Did they include any food? Yeah, they had a cafeteria on the boat, but like in all day picnics people used to bring their own baskets. Uh huh.
